title: Handley Page Halifax NR287
memorial_details:
description: Plaque: HERE ON MARCH 15th 1945 FELL/ A HALIFAX BOMBER RETURNING / FROM AN OPERATIONAL FLIGHT./ THE FOLLOWING MEMBERS/ OF THE CREW WERE KILLED./ (Names)/  

Scroll: 347 (Tunisie) Sqn/ This plaque is a memorial to five Free French Airmen killed as they/ returned to their base at Elvington from their thirty eighth and last/ mission. Unable to land due to a build up of other returning aircraft they/ flew north to await their turn to land. HALIFAX NR 287 LB-C (Charles) fate/ was sealed when, with damaged instruments and zero visibility, it struck a/ stone wall strewing debris across the fields./ The Halifax spilled out two of its occupants as it slithered and bounced its/ way across the earth, it punched its way through another wall and/ became airborne for a few hundred yards before finally being brought rest/ against a tree on farmland about half a mile from this church. Only the/ Flight Engineer and Rear Gunner escaped, though badly injured from/ the wreckage. For some years the plaque was attached to the tree against/ which the Halifax came to rest until the tree fell and the plaque was/ removed to the church porch here in Scawton./ Lest we Forget
